changelog: Align native builder owner resolution with the skill-driven generic-primitive architecture: supported builders can execute through their mandatory playbook even when no dedicated builder writer is installed.
Expose primitive_execution_supported and execution_mode in frontend owner resolution while preserving exact-target ownership and surface-resolution safety.
Keep Site Profile v2 inventory and multi-builder detection compatible with the gateway owner_hint, receipt and verification contracts.

items: Align native builder owner resolution with the skill-driven generic-primitive architecture: supported builders can execute through their mandatory playbook even when no dedicated builder writer is installed.
Expose primitive_execution_supported and execution_mode in frontend owner resolution while preserving exact-target ownership and surface-resolution safety.
Keep Site Profile v2 inventory and multi-builder detection compatible with the gateway owner_hint, receipt and verification contracts.
Add a persistent Site Profile v2 generated by the WordPress heartbeat, including active plugins, detected builders, theme, PHP and WordPress versions, multisite and permalink context.
Expose compact ecosystem signals for WooCommerce/HPOS, custom fields, forms, SEO and snippet systems so CodeAgent can use skills and generic primitives without rediscovering the site on every task.
Keep builder detection and active-plugin inventory lightweight and bounded while preserving the existing signed heartbeat and update compatibility.
Fix Bricks storage verification to read the physical postmeta row instead of stale metadata cache.
Detect 4-byte UTF-8 storage incompatibility deterministically and expose the real database cause instead of blind writer retries.
Harden Bricks persistence diagnostics so failed writes stop immediately with actionable storage evidence.
Adds safe WordPress administrator reauthorization for signed-v2 installations without disconnecting, re-pairing, or changing installation identity.
Keeps suspended recovery fail-closed when the CodeAgent resource is not active.
Surfaces the current transport failure instead of stale relay errors and adds an explicit reauthorization action in WordPress admin.
Prevent Imunify360/ImunifyAV false-positive cleanup from removing apply-php by delegating execution to the shared PHP runtime.
Keep the WordPress Abilities registry deterministic and complete; apply CodeAgent visibility at relay catalog/execution instead of unregistering abilities.
Preserve WooCommerce primitive-union compatibility and same-resource runtime filesystem fallbacks.
Harden the WordPress Abilities registry guard with exact wp_get_ability checks and self-heal critical same-resource runtime fallbacks before catalog/execution.
Verify the complete public CodeAgent ability registry stays aligned with relay and Admin catalogs, while preserving emergency synthetic tools separately.
Replace primitive WooCommerce oneOf unions with WordPress REST-compatible type unions for coupons, bulk pricing/stock selectors, and product category/tag selectors.
Make the deterministic layout verifier honor applicable attribute selectors and CSS max-width constraints before reporting fixed-width overflow.
Prevent false mobile/tablet overflow failures for responsive Bricks containers constrained by the native max-width:100% rule.
Keep mandatory frontend verification fail-closed while improving geometry evidence accuracy.
Add deterministic browserless layout-geometry verification across desktop, tablet and mobile projections.
Detect global overflow masking, viewport-breaking fixed dimensions, impossible grid minima and hidden verification roots with bounded clipping warnings.
Expose verify-layout-geometry as a dedicated read-only frontend evidence capability for mandatory builder verification.
Separate WPCodeBox2 persistent-snippet safety from immediate manual/run-once execution safety.
Allow existing persistent WordPress runtime behavior such as redirects, exit/die, HTTP calls, headers and wp_mail without false-positive activation or update blocks.
Keep the strict unsafe-pattern denylist for immediate manual/run-once execution, where CodeAgent executes code directly.
Add a regression contract that prevents live WPCodeBox snippets from inheriting the manual-run denylist again.
Fix Bricks residual CSS for bounded text-stroke and same-element state classes.
Allow signed public WordPress abilities from discovered namespaces through the tunnel.
Keep source-driven Bricks writes chunked by logical sections with exact per-chunk SVG and residual CSS scopes.
Restricts Bricks, Elementor and Gutenberg owner-specific site/build skills to runtimes where their native owner is actually available.
Compacts legacy auto-managed CodeAgent memory entries and removes obsolete task-context/source-memory residue without touching user-managed durable memory.
Searches the complete bounded durable-memory store and preserves upsert-by-name behavior even when the store is at capacity.
Preserves the WordPress option-control hardening prepared in this release line.
WordPress option tools now allow every non-sensitive option for authorized administrators instead of requiring a static allowlist, so core settings such as blog_public can be managed directly.
Credential, secret and installation-identity options remain protected, and update-option still requires the WordPress manage_options capability.
Fixes the PHP 8.1 fatal in the Bricks native revision writer by replacing the PHP 8.2-only literal true return type with a PHP 8.1-compatible boolean union.
Raises the declared minimum PHP version to 8.1 so the release metadata matches the plugin's existing PHP 8.1 syntax and prevents installation on unsupported PHP 8.0 runtimes.
Adds a source compatibility contract that blocks future PHP 8.2-only literal true/readonly-class syntax while the plugin minimum remains below PHP 8.2.
Builder Design Foundation now carries real native site geometry and unit context before material visual writes.
Bricks uses 1rem = 10px by default unless explicit current-site root-font evidence overrides it, and no longer assumes the browser 16px rem baseline.
Bricks, Elementor and Gutenberg foundation snapshots include their native container, layout, breakpoint, typography and global design signals and are reused for the builder session.
Visual references remain the composition authority without discarding the target site's native geometry and unit constraints.
Adds a short-lived task-bound authenticated WordPress browser session for draft and private frontend work without storing WordPress passwords or permanent login cookies.
Keeps the browser session read-only and isolated to the exact task target: GET/HEAD only, no wp-admin, REST or XML-RPC, one-time signed bootstrap and a maximum 10-minute lifetime.
Fixes Bricks draft template sessions by creating the browser bootstrap after WordPress and Bricks post types are registered, so the draft template itself remains the authenticated task target.
Includes the latest Bricks direct-target handling for blank draft documents and native template work.
New blank Bricks draft pages now resolve as direct native targets when their post type is enabled in Bricks.
Bricks routed-page work checks relevant template conditions before choosing the editable target and reuses that routing evidence until the target or conditions change.
Bricks page/template work now checks relevant template conditions once before the first material action, then reuses resolved routing evidence instead of rereading conditions on every task or call.
Routing conditions are re-read only when the target/template routing changes or prior evidence is stale; explicit template IDs remain authoritative.
- Adds codeagent.bricks-list-revisions for native Bricks/WordPress revision history, explicitly separate from private CodeAgent builder snapshots.
- Native Bricks revision list/create/restore are self-targeting revision lifecycle capabilities and no longer require the ordinary frontend authoring receipt.
- Keeps native restore on the Bricks Apply + Save backend path with safety revision and exact read-back verification.

- Native Bricks revision restore now mirrors the Bricks Apply + Save backend path: Bricks Database read, native validation, exact-area persistence, wp_update_post/save_post CSS lifecycle, and Bricks read-back verification.
- Native Bricks revision create/restore no longer enter the generic frontend authoring context or residual CSS scope flow.
- Restore always creates a native safety revision first and cannot fall back to bricks-set-content, generic post/meta/source writers, or private builder snapshots.
- Makes native Bricks revision create/restore capabilities semantically discoverable instead of exact-only.

- Adds audited semantic contracts so explicit revision restore/rollback requests resolve to codeagent.bricks-restore-revision rather than generic WordPress revision or private builder snapshot recovery.
- Requires native frontend context for Bricks revision mutations while preserving existing safety-revision and read-back verification behavior.
Adds native Bricks revision creation for pages and Bricks templates, producing real WordPress/Bricks revisions that appear in the native Bricks revision history.
Adds native Bricks revision restore with strict parent/area validation, automatic pre-restore safety revision, native content validation, CSS regeneration and verified read-back.
Extends Bricks capability discovery, manifest and admin catalog contracts so revision create/restore are first-class Bricks tools without changing existing builder workflows.
Aligns the WordPress admin interface with the current conturi.codeagent.ro design system, including the dark CodeAgent sidebar and dashboard hierarchy.
Brings dashboard cards, panels, controls, settings, memory and responsive behavior into the same restrained platform visual language without changing plugin capabilities or connection behavior.
Keeps the redesign isolated in a dedicated admin platform stylesheet for clean maintenance and rollback.
Aligns the WordPress admin with the global CodeAgent MCP endpoint and Working Scope, removing the legacy per-site connector and Claude setup from the primary UI.
Separates the internal signed WordPress relay from the public AI-client MCP endpoint and migrates existing installations to platform_mcp_url without changing site identity or transport.

Keeps resource isolation and transport compatibility while reporting CodeAgent site connection state accurately and preventing internal downstream MCP URLs from being presented as client setup endpoints.

Strengthens Bricks layout fidelity: CTA groups preserve evidenced axis/alignment/gap, recurring decorative treatments remain one semantic pattern, and shown anchored/overlapping compositions are realized explicitly instead of flattened into default flow.

Adds bounded conversion-context consistency for equivalent benefit indicators and sales-page trust elements while forbidding invented overlaps or guessed offsets; these remain evidence-driven design defaults rather than structural shortcuts.

Keeps the newer Bricks coherent-write/responsive fast path and exact visual-reference authority, expands the public Bricks ability profile for component creation and patch-elements, and makes list-elements catalog cardinality explicit.

Bricks multi-section construction now prefers one coherent native document/composition write when the requested tree is already known, with realistic payload budgets and multiple root Sections instead of section-by-section write/verify loops.

All 65 Bricks capabilities keep the 3.5.58 contract hardening and now expose workflow lanes; core construction writers are prioritized, visual component creation is frontend-context bound, and capability inventory is authorized/primary-first.

Bricks verification and responsive realization are consolidated after the final material write unless a real dependency requires intermediate state; redundant design-context preflight is no longer mandatory when frontend_context already carries sufficient evidence.
Hardens all 65 Bricks capabilities with a canonical owner/resource/operation/tier matrix so discovery no longer depends on name similarity or oversized descriptions.
Closes every Bricks public input-schema root fail-closed while preserving provider-native dynamic maps such as element settings and live control payloads.

Preserves Bricks frontend-context and orchestration metadata end-to-end, hides schema/routing helpers from broad discovery, and keeps exact Bricks contracts compact while retaining authoritative schemas on exact load.

Adds native WooCommerce Order Metrics aggregation for order_count and gross_total, including HPOS-safe server-side filtering by status, currency and relative/date windows without returning order rows or customer PII.

Separates order-row listing from aggregate metrics and declares exact discovery operations such as sum_totals/gross_total/order_count so capability routing does not use list-orders for aggregation requests.
Hardens capability matching and completion: specific structured operations require declared operation coverage, and a mismatched simple-read capability cannot auto-complete the requested outcome.
Adds a live Bricks Theme Style control-schema capability so CodeAgent uses exact native keys such as typographyHeadingH2:mobile_landscape instead of semantic aliases that Bricks silently ignores.

Theme Style create/edit now validates only the controls supplied by the current write, rejects unknown control keys and breakpoints deterministically, and preserves unrelated legacy state for bounded corrections.

Strengthens the Bricks playbook: discover exact Theme Style keys when needed, continue native global typography changes after explicit approval, and verify generated Bricks CSS rather than treating saved-but-inert settings as success.

Resolves Bricks-routed WordPress posts, pages, and custom singular post types through the exact rendered content template, so article URLs can rebind to their native Bricks Single/content template instead of failing as unsupported.

Treats an explicit user approval of a shared/global typography option as scope authority for the exact native Bricks Theme Style change; the playbook now continues natively and forbids CSS/PHP/non-playbook fallback for capability-plumbing errors.

Publishes Theme Style mutation metadata and keeps native Bricks semantic grouping plus Section(root) -> Container -> Block structure guidance synchronized across the WordPress and native CodeAgent packages.
Enforces the Bricks page/template surface hierarchy Section(root) -> Container -> Block -> content as a hard structural contract.

Rejects nested Sections, non-Container direct Section children, and content elements placed directly under the surface Container while preserving local component internals below the required Block layer.

Aligns Bricks element discovery and insert-writer guidance with the hard hierarchy and adds regression coverage for the exact Block -> Section / direct-content-under-Container failure shown in the builder tree.
Fixes semantic and SEO readiness attachment to the computed frontend structure result.
Resolves the WordPress post from a public permalink so published indexability and Article schema checks are evaluated correctly.
Keeps the cross-builder typography hierarchy and responsive consistency checks introduced in 3.5.52.
Adds cross-builder typography hierarchy and responsive line-height quality advisories for Bricks and Elementor.
Adds deterministic semantic and SEO readiness evidence to frontend structure verification.
Keeps SEO metadata and schema provider-native and prevents generic keyword or schema shortcuts.
Elementor Playbook v3: native owner lifecycle, bounded site fingerprint, layout-generation awareness, design consistency and responsive completion rules.
Adds native Elementor Theme Builder template inventory plus display-condition read/write through Elementor Pro Conditions_Manager.
Theme Builder routing now detects overlapping active conditions before mutation and fails closed when native conflict inspection or routing is unavailable.
Adds Builder Playbook Contract v3 with strict separation between WordPress content entities and native builder visual surfaces, including targetless native creation and safe lineage rebind.

Expands the Bricks site playbook with bounded design-context fingerprinting, native reuse hierarchy, dynamic template behavior, routing-conflict safety, responsive realization, and deterministic completion evidence.
Adds and hardens native visual-surface creation paths across Bricks, Elementor, and Gutenberg while failing closed instead of falling back to generic WordPress content, HTML, PHP, or another builder.
Resolves the active routed Bricks template from its exact generated post-{template_id}.css stylesheet before falling back to shared element-ID fingerprints.
Separates strong generated-stylesheet owner evidence from weak element-fingerprint evidence so cloned WooCommerce product templates no longer create false ambiguity.
Allows product-specific wc_product surfaces to resolve deterministically when multiple Bricks templates share the same cloned element IDs.

Separates the requested WooCommerce product/page from the actual editable Bricks render surface, resolves the active wc_product template, and classifies routing impact as single or shared before any native write is exposed.

Adds native bricks-duplicate-template for safe per-product forks of shared Bricks templates: source content/type are cloned, global routing is not inherited implicitly, and new conditions require explicit routing authorization.

Hardens Bricks template/content operations with runtime-aware template types, full-area set-content CAS, corrected capability provenance, and fail-closed shared-surface handling so local tasks cannot silently mutate a global product template.

Creates Bricks templates from the active runtime template-type catalog, including WooCommerce types such as wc_product when the installed Bricks runtime exposes them, instead of freezing only the core template types.

Lets bricks-create-template apply an explicitly authorized native Bricks condition set atomically during template creation, avoiding content-template, raw-meta, and global-template routing workarounds.
Fixes the Bricks template-conditions catalog entry so the public writer resolves to its actual set-template-conditions implementation.

Makes signed CodeAgent draft/private previews bind the WordPress main request to the exact authorized post ID, post type, and current post status before WP_Query, preventing authenticated builder drafts from falling through to theme-level 404 routing.
Keeps preview authority fail-closed: the request binding activates only after the installation signature, exact target, administrator authority, and edit capability have already been verified.
Preserves the 3.5.45 browser-independent verification architecture and authenticated deterministic HTML/DOM/CSS evidence lane.

Retires the browser-dependent frontend runtime probe and keeps JavaScript evidence site-owned through the connected WordPress plugin; CodeAgent no longer depends on a central Node, Chromium, Playwright, or external page-opening runtime for frontend verification.

Adds signed authenticated post_id preview to deterministic frontend HTML, DOM structure, DOM compare, CSS-owner, and JavaScript source inspection so draft/private targets can be verified as the connector-authorizing WordPress administrator without publishing.

Makes material frontend completion evidence-based: native builder save/read-back and verify-state prove persistence only, while the agent must continue to deterministic post-write site evidence before claiming a visual task is complete.
Hardens the CodeAgent update supply chain with detached manifest signatures and mandatory SHA-256 verification of downloaded plugin packages before installation.
Separates stable and testing update channels while preserving stable as the default and keeping the existing updater filters compatible.
Cleans production packages by excluding tests, backups and development artifacts, and adds source-test and release-hygiene gates before publication.

changes: Moves JavaScript inspection off CodeAgent server-side Node/happy-dom execution: codeagent.inspect-js now runs bounded static same-origin inspection locally in the connected WordPress plugin.

Adds codeagent.run-js-event-test as a short-lived real-browser plugin probe for listeners, dispatches, jQuery, dataLayer, console/runtime errors, fetch/XHR, DOM geometry, computed CSS, mutations and safe synthetic form events.
Keeps runtime traces bounded and redacted, gates active probes to an exact capture id/path, and prevents synthetic click/submit diagnostics from invoking native navigation or form submission.
Keeps the exact Bricks area rollback introduced in 3.5.41 and adds pre-write proof for manual element restores, so an ambiguous surgical rollback is rejected before changing builder storage.
Prevents the replaced-root edge case from reinserting the old subtree beside an unknown replacement and only discovering the mismatch after mutation.
Retains snapshot state v2 placement hashing, normalization-free exact recovery writes, transactional CAS, CSS regeneration, and exact read-back verification.
Makes automatic Bricks recovery area-scoped so rollback owns every persisted change caused by area-wide selector/signature normalization and root-id replacement.

Restores Bricks snapshots through a dedicated exact recovery writer that bypasses normal builder normalization, uses transactional current-state CAS, regenerates CSS, and verifies the captured state exactly.
Adds snapshot state v2 placement hashing and fail-closed surgical positioning so manual element rollback never reports success after guessing a different parent/sibling position.

Uses CodeAgent Design full templates/blocks as the composition source for material new-page, rebuild and redesign work; screenshot/image attachments are secondary visual guidance instead of page architecture.
Keeps supplied HTML/CSS/template/code as direct implementation source, including the deterministic compiled-source fast path when available.
Aligns the packaged frontend/design skills around one template-first hierarchy while preserving native builders, browserless verification, bounded custom gaps and AI-owned sequencing.
Makes bounded custom_element_scope consistent across the full Bricks validation pipeline: an explicitly authorized SVG/Code payload field is not re-rejected by the generic raw-markup scanner.
The exemption applies only to the exact scoped custom element payload field; all other settings and all unscoped raw markup remain validated and blocked normally.
Supports the deterministic static-source Bricks fast path without weakening native-editability or raw HTML safety boundaries.
Adds bounded custom_element_scope support to Bricks replace-content so exact inline SVG artwork can be preserved in a native subtree replacement without widening to raw HTML or full-page code.
Keeps raw HTML/Code blocked and requires the custom scope to exactly match the SVG code elements in the bounded write.
Enables the central static-source fast path to use the same deterministic Bricks validation boundary while older adapters safely fall back to the existing AI-owned path.
Marks responsive/native composition quality messages explicitly as advisories so successful native builder writes cannot be promoted into correction loops by generic warning text.
Removes the dead legacy-policy-js test tree that referenced the retired automatic frontend-design skill router and was outside the active test glob.

Keeps frontend correction escalation only for deterministic evidence that requested output was stripped, dropped, not realized, missing, broken, or rendered incorrectly; generic layout/fallback wording no longer triggers recovery.

Removes retired builder-policy error contracts from active runtime: native_component_underuse, responsive_realization_required, and obsolete gateway catalog/preflight error handling no longer participate in execution or recovery decisions.

Bricks Section/Container, responsive composition, and component-usage heuristics now use advisory-shaped APIs and messages end to end, eliminating WP_Error-shaped quality signals that future callers could accidentally hard-block.
Elementor responsive and component-usage quality signals now return plain advisories instead of WP_Error objects; deterministic schema/control/render safety remains enforced separately.
Renames stale hard-invariant/version-stamped regression contracts to safety/advisory contracts and keeps only negative assertions for retired identifiers so old architecture cannot silently return.

changelog: Adds a state-bound completed-replay contract for capabilities whose correct outcome depends on changing runtime state, preventing stale self-update receipts from masking a newly available CodeAgent version.
The WordPress relay now exposes bounded replay_policy metadata; managed self-update binds that policy to the currently installed CodeAgent version while retaining exact-once operation receipts.
Keeps native-builder autonomy fixes intact and adds regression coverage for state-bound replay semantics.

items: Aligns the Bricks builder profile with the 3.5.32 autonomy policy so frontend_context no longer advertises native div as forbidden or Section->Container/Block as absolute structure.
Bricks context now exposes Container and Block as preferences, native div as valid, native-first ownership, and bounded custom_element_scope only for a concrete native capability gap.
Adds regression coverage preventing stale builder-profile policy from reintroducing orchestration retries after validator de-rigidity.

Builder autonomy: Bricks and Elementor composition, primitive-ratio and responsive heuristics are now advisories instead of hard blockers; deterministic invalidity and unsafe persistence still fail closed.

Bricks native composition is no longer forced into Section -> Container or Block-only shapes; native div and legitimate full-bleed/direct structures remain valid, and grid gaps no longer trigger false flex-display failures.
Native widgets remain the default when they semantically match the requested component; unrelated widgets are never forced to satisfy component-count heuristics.
Adds bounded Bricks custom_element_scope for exact native capability gaps while keeping raw HTML/code unavailable as a shortcut for otherwise native builder work.

Updates builder skills and regression contracts to preserve source-driven native reconstruction, responsive QA, persistence verification and flattened-composite protections without workflow bureaucracy.
Bricks patch read-back now normalizes %root% to the persisted #brxe-element selector before comparing residual CSS, eliminating false patch_not_persisted failures.
Keeps 3.5.30's strictly whitelisted visual-only residual CSS support for native control gaps without opening layout, spacing, sizing, positioning or responsive CSS shortcuts.
Adds regression coverage for resolved residual CSS selector persistence during targeted Bricks patches.
Bricks residual CSS now supports strictly whitelisted root-level visual effects when current native controls cannot express the requested design.
Root-level residual CSS remains blocked for layout, sizing, spacing, positioning, typography sizing, responsive rules, external assets and general styling shortcuts.
Adds contract coverage for gradients, blur/backdrop-filter, shadows and clipped text effects while preserving native-first builder ownership.
Bounded Bricks edits now ignore unrelated pre-existing legacy validation debt and reject only new validation errors introduced by the current scoped mutation.
Patch, insert, remove, move and bounded subtree replacement keep native validation for the changed outcome while full-area replacements still validate the complete document.
Prevents small Bricks edits from entering page-wide legacy cleanup loops or expiring frontend context before the intended save.
Simplifies frontend orchestration so the AI owns sequencing, mutation granularity, correction and semantic completion end to end.
Removes fixed clear/preserve and section-by-section workflow gates from frontend runtime, builder skills and writer guidance; optional plan and trace labels never authorize or block execution.
Frontend context now exposes native target, owner, current state and capabilities with workflow_gate=none and AI-selected mutation granularity.
Keeps hard technical safety where it belongs: resource and owner isolation, authorization, concurrency, payload validation, deduplication, ambiguity protection and authoritative evidence.
Reduces unnecessary discovery and schema loops while preserving coherent native subtree writes and same-owner recovery when validation actually needs correction.
Keeps frontend workflow semantics AI-owned: CodeAgent consumes a structured semantic plan and never derives replacement mode or ordering from request wording.
Adds explicit clear_then_build execution: the native content area must be cleared and verified empty before the first new section is written.
Keeps preserve_existing as the section-by-section path for redesigns that retain the current document structure.
Adds explicit empty-document support for Gutenberg semantic clear milestones while keeping ordinary empty writes fail-closed.
Aligns Bricks, Elementor, Gutenberg and shared builder guidance with ordered semantic milestones and one final cross-document verification.
Makes material multi-section frontend builds persist exactly one semantic root section per mutation call, in document order.
Existing-page redesigns replace root sections atomically one by one; new or empty pages insert one root section at a time instead of holding a giant unsaved page payload.
Whole-document Bricks, Elementor and Gutenberg writers are now exception-only and are no longer marked single-call preferred for ordinary full-page redesigns.

Each section writer uses its own validation, persistence and read-back as the milestone; one final cross-document native verification runs after the last section instead of verifying after every write.
Keeps section writes coarse enough to avoid element-by-element tool-call churn while allowing a section to split only when materially large, risky or carrying a high-risk native component.
Retires public Chromium/Playwright frontend verification; draft/private frontend completion now uses native builder state, generated output semantics and server-side safety checks.
Fixes Bricks multi-select schema/value handling: controls with multiple=true are described as arrays and scalar values are rejected before persistence.
Adds a native Bricks render-safety preflight before every structural write so malformed candidate trees cannot take the frontend down with a PHP Throwable.
Compacts Bricks element discovery by de-duplicating only true base controls while preserving element-specific underscore controls such as _objectFit.
Makes return_css useful with Bricks file CSS by returning bounded generated-file evidence with SHA-256, byte count and source metadata instead of an empty string.
Published frontend verification keeps bounded HTML, computed structure, DOM compare and find-css-owner evidence without automated browser execution.
Makes Bricks responsive validation intrinsic-layout aware: vertical stacks, auto-fit/minmax grids and mobile-hidden navigation groups no longer require redundant breakpoint overrides.
Blocks Bricks flex controls without _display:flex before persistence, preventing successful writes that Bricks would silently degrade.

Compacts Bricks native schema discovery by de-duplicating shared controls and truncating oversized option lists; frontend context now carries the native catalog fingerprint so full rebuilds do not need a broad catalog call.
Adds signed draft/private frontend preview v3 that resolves the current WordPress authority locally, removing stale central user-id drift while preserving exact target/persona verification.
Fixes canonical Project Memory upsert_by_name so automatic verified writeback updates in one operation instead of duplicate-search-retry ping-pong.
Binds managed self-update exact-once identity to the currently installed CodeAgent version so a new release is never hidden by a prior successful self-update receipt.
Includes refreshable deterministic builder-validation receipts and intrinsic vertical Bricks responsiveness fixes.
Releases legacy completed invalid_elements receipts during operation begin so corrected native builder payloads can be reevaluated after runtime upgrades.
Uses one central refreshable-validation classifier for begin/finalize exact-once behavior.
Allows deterministic pre-persistence native validation failures to be reevaluated instead of replaying a stale failed exact-once receipt.
Preserves exact-once receipts for successful, ambiguous, in-flight, and generic writer outcomes.
Allows explicitly vertical native Bricks flex stacks to satisfy responsive realization without redundant breakpoint overrides.
Adds bounded same-owner builder schema/catalog reads to frontend context receipts so full-page/reference rebuilds can validate native controls without rediscovery.

Hardens native frontend execution receipts to the exact owner, target area, focused element and bounded writer set; degraded frontend context now performs the required native read internally before any write is exposed.
Adds fail-closed optimistic concurrency and transactional persistence for Bricks, including atomic multi-page component deletion with multi-target recovery instead of partial orphan cleanup.
Extends scoped recovery to progressive Bricks/Elementor writers and Gutenberg post content, with content-hash preconditions so stale writes and rollback over newer work are rejected.
Serializes Elementor Global Classes, Variables and v3 global-style mutations against the active Kit to reduce lost-update races during concurrent editor/API saves.
Fixes Gutenberg adapter detection for the exact target post type and closes partial/orphan failure paths in Bricks template creation and related native writes.
Focused frontend context now fails closed when an annotated Elementor or Bricks element no longer exists, returning an explicit stale-target error instead of continuing with empty target context.
Preserves the deterministic annotation handoff and compact targeted-edit fast path introduced in 3.5.17 while preventing stale visual annotations from being applied to guessed replacement elements.

Adds deterministic workflow handoff for single native visual annotations, carrying the exact WordPress post, builder owner and element into focused frontend context without repeated semantic discovery.

Adds focused frontend context for already-identified Elementor/Bricks targets so targeted edits return only the exact element, minimal parent/runtime evidence and bounded native writers instead of a broad page/design payload.

Moves frontend-render-inspect to exact-only discovery so the expensive browser renderer no longer competes with ordinary native builder reads/writes; browser QA remains available as an explicit escalation.
Fixes CodeAgent private recovery storage discovery on common managed-hosting layouts by preferring the hosting account private directory before the sibling hidden-directory fallback.

Managed CodeAgent update/recovery checkpoints can now use a writable path outside the public webroot on ISPConfig-style accounts while preserving the existing webroot escape guards and 0700 directory hardening.
Restores CodeAgent visual frontend annotations in the WordPress Admin Bar with a lightweight element selector, right-side drawer and authenticated WordPress storage.

Restores the public annotation MCP workflow with annotations-review, annotations-get and annotations-apply-start, and adds annotations-apply-complete with guarded pending/in-progress/applied/failed/dismissed state transitions.

Captures native Bricks, Elementor and Gutenberg target hints so annotation work routes through the canonical builder owner; Bricks frontend brxe-* element IDs are resolved to their native element IDs.
Adds package and skill-family integrity contracts so declared first-party capabilities cannot silently ship without their implementation files.
Responsive validation is now risk-based: fluid native vertical layouts no longer require artificial breakpoint overrides.
Elementor and Bricks still fail closed for concrete row/grid/multi-column reflow risks and oversized typography without native responsive realization.
Release contracts are version-agnostic and keep Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and other MCP clients on the same provider-neutral runtime contract.
Combină validarea live a controalelor Bricks din 3.5.12 cu hard gate-ul responsive: layouturile materiale Elementor/Bricks desktop-only sunt respinse înainte de persist.
Adaugă protecție Elementor pentru sesiuni editor concurente prin edit-lock, astfel încât un tab Elementor deschis să nu mai poată suprascrie modificările CodeAgent.

Unifică design-intelligence, design-system și skill-urile builder în aceeași sursă de release, cu grupare semantică, componente native, referințe read-only și breakpoint-uri desktop/tablet/mobile obligatorii.
Păstrează validarea Bricks pe lifecycle-ul nativ al controalelor și catalogul live, inclusiv respingerea cheilor inexistente înainte de salvare.
Validarea Bricks folosește acum lifecycle-ul nativ complet al controalelor (`set_controls_before` → controlul elementului → `set_controls_after`) în locul unei liste statice incomplete.

Controale native de bază precum `_overflow`, poziționare, sizing și celelalte controale comune sunt recunoscute corect per element, în timp ce chei inexistente precum `_gridColumn` continuă să fie respinse înainte de persist.
Catalogul exact al unui element expune acum aceleași controale live folosite de validator, iar copy-style folosește numai controalele CSS reale ale elementului.
Bricks writer-ele resping acum înainte de salvare cheile de control inexistente, inclusiv cheile de layout/style care încep cu underscore.
Validarea responsive verifică și breakpoint-ul real; valori precum _gridColumn sau breakpoint-uri inventate nu mai pot trece ca persisted fără efect frontend.
Patch-urile pe elemente legacy validează doar setările noi/modificate, astfel încât datele vechi necorelate nu blochează editări sigure.
Elementor source-reference rebuilds now resolve inline SVGs as sanitized, deduplicated WordPress attachments instead of invalid data URLs.
Source SVG dependencies are injected only after the native tree validates, then the resolved tree is validated again before persistence.
Font and SVG dependencies are rollback-safe when validation or page persistence fails.
Native source compilation normalizes unsupported CSS forms before they reach the Elementor v4 Style Schema.
HTML/CSS reference rebuilds can now use deterministic native-builder source plans instead of model-authored layout reconstruction.
Elementor v4 tree writers preserve authored desktop/tablet/mobile responsive variants without persisting viewport-measured hard widths.
Source font dependencies are applied through the Elementor Kit after validation and rolled back if the page write fails.
Source-design compilation preserves authored CSS evidence and no longer stalls on motion-freeze injection.
Elementor v4 subtree writers now accept ergonomic breakpoint maps for desktop/tablet/mobile and compile them into native atomic style variants.
